author: lxx-translators

original.text: καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ φῶς ὅτι καλόν. καὶ διεχώρισεν ὁ θεὸς ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ φωτὸς καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σκότους.

english.text: And God saw the light, that it was beautiful. And God separated between the light and between the darkness.

notes: Two features of the Greek decide most of what the Latin bench can say. First, the Hebrew ki tov is rendered kalon, 'beautiful' rather than 'good' — so that the approval reads as an aesthetic verdict, which is what Ambrose then expounds at length and what Augustine has to argue is not a verdict reached after the event. Second, the Hebrew's bein … u-vein is carried over word for word as ana meson … kai ana meson, 'between … and between', and the Old Latin that Augustine and his Carolingian copyists read reproduces it as divisit inter lucem et tenebras. Jerome does not: he writes divisit lucem a tenebris. Which of the two a Latin witness quotes is the cleanest single indication of which Latin text lay in front of him, and on this verse the two texts sort the bench almost perfectly.
